{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.320","Changelog":"v1.0.4.322 (2026-10-28) [testing]
- **BossMod status checks survive a missing or half-loaded BossMod.** Upstream WrathCombo reorganized its BossMod IPC into shared helpers with null-safe fallbacks; that rework (d9c63e468) is merged, so the active-preset module walk, autorotation, custom-queueing, smart-target and AI-targeting checks answer false cleanly when BossMod's rotation window or action queue is absent, instead of erroring partway through the walk.
- BossMod Reborn keeps being read through its own IPC (active preset verdict, AI targeting, manual-queue setting); those reads are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.321 (2026-10-27) [testing]
- **BossMod conflict detection works with current BossMod builds again.** BossMod moved its rotation manager and action-module queue underneath a new window object, so the checks that read the original BossMod's active preset, AI targeting and manual-queue setting found nothing and the preset, AI-targeting and manual-queue verdicts silently came back empty. Those reflection reads now follow the new location, and upstream WrathCombo's matching fix (54e36f2f) is merged; BossMod Reborn keeps being read through its own IPC and is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.320 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is back, now fenced so the cleanse scan can never hang or spin a frame.** Same cleanse behaviour as before the withdrawal: dispellable debuffs are graded by worth (movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer can spare the cast, damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs never take one, doom always, the dead never), hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere, and one debuff can never consume two casts. New in this build, the cleanse scan runs behind a frame guard: it pauses right after a plugin reload and right after any territory change (the two windows the withdrawn build ran into trouble in), can never re-enter itself, and if a single scan ever costs more than a frame the plugin logs the managed call stack at the slow point and stands the scan down for two seconds instead of repeating next tick.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.319 withdrawal build. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.319 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is withdrawn; cleanse behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.317 behaviour.** The change graded dispellable debuffs by worth, required friendly targets along the Esuna retargeting chain and held a second cleanse back while a first was still resolving, but a full game freeze was reported with the build present, the main thread spinning inside the plugin's own managed code, and the exact looping path could not be established from the captured evidence. The whole change comes out rather than leave a suspected hazard on the heal path: the retargeting chain, the worth checks and the double-cast window of v1.0.4.317 are restored as they were.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.318 testing build, which is withdrawn. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.318 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **Automatic cleanses (Esuna and Exuviation) now fire only when the debuff is worth the cast, and never twice for the same debuff.** Three defects fixed at one shared verdict. First, the Esuna retargeting chain could resolve a hostile target: a mob carrying its own dispel-flagged damage-over-time effect (for example Combust III on the mob the DoT was cast on) outranked the real party member, so grinding a FATE could spend global cooldowns casting Esuna at a mob. The chain now requires a friendly target at every step, and hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere. Second, the heal-combo cleanse branch and the auto-rotation's party cleanse were two independent casters for the same debuff while the status list still showed a debuff that a cast already in flight was removing, so one debuff could consume two casts seconds apart. Every cleanse send now goes through one shared verdict that remembers a cleanse sent in the last few seconds and stands down until it resolves. Third, every dispellable status was treated as equally worth a cast. The verdict now grades them: movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, because cleansing them is the dodge; damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer is healthy enough to spare the cast; damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs that fall off on their own never take one. Under low health only a cleansing doom is still worth the cast, and a dead candidate is never targeted.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.317 (2026-10-21) [testing]
- **The Cast-Start Stillness setting is removed, together with the v1.0.4.316 testing build it shipped in.** That build held a fresh cast bar for a moment after movement stopped to keep the bar from being glued onto a dodge, but casting into a stop is normal cast mechanics, not a stuck slide-cast, so the hold answered a problem the game does not have. Cast-start movement behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.315 behaviour: moving always blocks a new cast start, instant casts and orbwalker-driven movement never block, and a stopped player casts immediately. The v1.0.4.315 FATE-grind spike skip is untouched. A settings file that still carries the old key loads unchanged; the key is ignored and disappears at the next save.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.316 testing build, which is withdrawn. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]

- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The click behavior, the confirming second click and everything else in the previous build are unchanged.

v0.0.3.5 (2026-10-05) [testing]

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Market Helper","Punchline":"Undercut, list, gather and buy — market board automation end to end.","Description":"Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with five tabs:

UNDERCUT — Walk a summoning bell's retainers and undercut every listed item. HQ and NQ are handled separately, your own retainers are matched rather than undercut, per-item overrides and price memory are supported, an obvious troll price is skipped, and mannequin/display items are never touched (if a row can't be verified it is skipped rather than risk delisting it). Closes the bell when it finishes.

LISTER — Build a list (hold CTRL and hover an item, or search) and press Go to list them all. Prices each item at the most common market price, ignoring lone troll listings, against your world, data center or whole region. Per-item stack sizes and list amounts, rolls extra items to the next retainer at the 20-slot cap, and includes a no-touch dry run.

FLIPPER — Compare any marketable item across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modelling.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. If a planned listing has already been bought it chases the next cheapest, on other worlds if needed, until your order is filled. Dry run is on by default.

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

01daabc: fix(FaloopIntegration): connect to Faloop's new Socket.IO endpoint

Faloop's frontend update (2026-10-30) moved the Socket.IO endpoint from
/comms/socket.io to the /legacy namespace on /messaging/socket.io/.
The old endpoint still accepts connections but no longer delivers mob
reports, so follow the new endpoint.

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]

- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]

- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The server info bar entry shows the boss FATE icon instead of the sword glyphs.** The same icon is used in every state; the bot's on/off state stays in the text (": On", ": Off" and the rest), exactly as before. No other entry is affected.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The click behavior, the confirming second click and everything else in the previous build are unchanged.

v0.0.3.5 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **Server info bar (Umbra) toggle for the FATE bot.** The plugin adds a "Lazy Fate Automation" entry to the game's server info bar, which Umbra renders as a button. It shows the bot state with the sibling entries' sword icon: On, Off, "(stopping)" while a soft stop is pending, or the live state such as "Paused (in instance)". Clicking it stops the bot (Ctrl+click waits for the current FATE to finish, like the window's soft stop); when stopped, the first click arms the start and a second click within 10 seconds confirms it, so a stray click cannot start the automation. - New display setting "Show server info bar entry" (on by default) hides or shows the entry; it can also be hidden per-plugin in Umbra or under /xlsettings -> Server Info Bar.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. FATEs above your level are now skipped; the tracker's unavailable list shows "FATE level N is above your level M". FATEs at or below your level run exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The server info bar entry shows the boss FATE icon instead of the sword glyphs.** The same icon is used in every state; the bot's on/off state stays in the text (": On", ": Off" and the rest), exactly as before. No other entry is affected.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The click behavior, the confirming second click and everything else in the previous build are unchanged.

v0.0.3.5 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **Server info bar (Umbra) toggle for the FATE bot.** The plugin adds a "Lazy Fate Automation" entry to the game's server info bar, which Umbra renders as a button. It shows the bot state with the sibling entries' sword icon: On, Off, "(stopping)" while a soft stop is pending, or the live state such as "Paused (in instance)". Clicking it stops the bot (Ctrl+click waits for the current FATE to finish, like the window's soft stop); when stopped, the first click arms the start and a second click within 10 seconds confirms it, so a stray click cannot start the automation. Starting still requires a logged-in character, exactly like the Lazy Hub switch.
- New display setting "Show server info bar entry" (on by default) hides or shows the entry; it can also be hidden per-plugin in Umbra or under /xlsettings -> Server Info Bar.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections.
